properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js provides the SHA-256/HMAC-SHA-256 consumed inside @walletconnect/crypto (which declares hash.js ^1.1.7) — the MAC half of the WalletConnect v1 session channel (AES-CBC via aes-js + HMAC via hash.js) that src/App.tsx's `new WalletConnect(...)` sessions rely on; elliptic and ethereum-cryptography also depend on it. Available in the shipped bundle even where first-party code never calls it directly.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The secp256k1 ECDSA curve is the Ethereum signing curve — the same curve this app's own wallet signs with via ethers and eth-sig-util (src/controllers/wallet.ts, all five sign* methods). Observable here, replaceable only by the Ethereum protocol: the curve is fixed by the chain, so ML-DSA migration is a protocol-level change, not an app-level one.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the shipped tree contains a single-round MD5 KDF. Reached only by transitive browser crypto polyfills (crypto-browserify/browserify-aes under react-scripts-ts webpack builds); no application code path uses it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: OpenBSD bcrypt_pbkdf KDF shipped via sshpk (http-signature → request chain in the react-scripts-ts dev-server toolchain). No application call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: node-forge RSA is shipped with the build toolchain (self-signed dev-server HTTPS). No RSA call site in the application; Shor-vulnerable primitive, ML-KEM-768 is the eventual replacement.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Purpose is JSON-RPC request/response correlation (the id field, used by apiSendTransaction in src/helpers/api.ts and the WalletConnect payload path), not key material — but predictable ids in a wallet's request path aid request-spoofing/replay against the bridge. Cheap fix: crypto.getRandomValues (already available via ethers.utils.randomBytes used at wallet.ts:85). First-party code, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: classical ECDH key agreement shipped in the browser polyfill layer of the react-scripts-ts/webpack toolchain; no application call site. Shor-relevant (retroactively breakable) though only reachable through browserify polyfills here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: Ed25519 capability ships with eth-sig-util's tweetnacl; the application never calls nacl.sign (wallet.ts only imports signTypedData_v4). Shor-vulnerable signature primitive; ML-DSA-65 is the migration target if ever used.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the ECDSA-secp256k1 engine actually exercised by this app: eth-sig-util@2.5.3's signTypedData_v4 is called at src/controllers/wallet.ts:217 for EIP-712 signing, and secp256k1@4.0.2 also depends on elliptic ^6.5.2. Quantum-unsafe under Shor; migration target ML-DSA-65, but the signature scheme is fixed by the Ethereum protocol itself, so replacement is observable-only at app level.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: X25519 ships inside eth-sig-util's nacl.box-based encrypt API; the app never calls encrypt (no encryption call anywhere in src/). Retroactively breakable key agreement if ever exercised; ML-KEM-768 hybrid is the migration target.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 is Ethereum's hashing workhorse: ethers' signing paths (wallet.signMessage/signTransaction in src/controllers/wallet.ts) and eth-sig-util's signTypedData_v4 (wallet.ts:217) hash with keccak256 before the secp256k1 ECDSA, and EIP-55 address checksums (ethers.utils.getAddress) are keccak-based. SHA-3/Keccak is not Shor-vulnerable (Grover square-root only), so this is an inventory fact, not an urgent migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 ships twice over: @ethersproject/pbkdf2 is used inside ethers' BIP-39 path — the very derivation this app's wallet.ts:95 (ethers.Wallet.fromMnemonic) exercises, BIP-39 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 at 2048 iterations — and the pbkdf2 npm package ships via the browserify crypto-shim stack (ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 declares pbkdf2 ^3.0.17). LIB-ea49d4c1 (Crypto dependency: pbkdf2@3.1.1) is one of these declared packages.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: scrypt feeds ethers v5's encrypted-JSON-keystore support (@ethersproject/json-wallets); the app does not export an encrypted keystore (no encrypt call in src/), but the KDF ships with the wallet library. Memory-hard, Grover-only quantum exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: AES ships inside node-forge for the dev-server cert toolchain; no AES call site in the application. Symmetric primitive, Grover-only exposure.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency inventory: the AE scheme available through eth-sig-util's nacl.box encrypt path; the application never calls it. 256-bit symmetric — quantum-safe against Grover.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: two copies ship. eth-sig-util's tweetnacl@1.0.3 backs its nacl.box encrypt helpers (never called by the app); sshpk's tweetnacl@0.14.5 backs its ed25519 key format support in the dev-server request chain. Either way, the provider is frozen and non-PQ; the secp256k1 ECDSA that the app actually uses comes from a different library entirely.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Crypto provider inventory: node-forge powers the self-signed dev-server HTTPS certificate in the react-scripts-ts toolchain (via selfsigned@1.10.7). No PQ capability; no application call site. Upgradeable here — bump the toolchain's dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PKI inventory: the self-signed cert guards only the local dev-server HTTPS listener; not production TLS posture. Changeable here via toolchain upgrade.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PKI inventory: X.509 handling ships with node-forge for the dev-server self-signed certificate chain (RSA-signed, classical). Not used for production trust.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt is the memory-hard KDF available in the shipped Ethereum crypto stack — ethers uses it for V3 keystore (web3 secret storage) encryption; this app never calls it directly, but it ships in the dependency tree and any future keystore import path would use it. Available in the shipped library; no first-party call site found in the application.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-1/SHA-2 streaming hash implementations pulled transitively by the browserify crypto-shim stack that the Ethereum packages use (create-hash/create-hmac consumers; sha.js ^2.4.x is declared at package-lock.json:4972, 4985, 13011, 28519, 35157). Available in the shipped bundle; no first-party call site — the app's own SHA-2/HMAC use happens inside ethers/@walletconnect.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the ECDSA-secp256k1 engine actually exercised by this app: eth-sig-util@2.5.3 declares elliptic ^6.4.0 (package-lock.json:6883), and WalletController.signTypedData (src/controllers/wallet.ts:217) calls eth-sig-util's signTypedData_v4 for EIP-712 signing — so this library performs live ECDSA secp256k1 signatures in the shipped bundle. Quantum-unsafe under Shor; ML-DSA-65 is the target, though the scheme is fixed by the Ethereum protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Generates the self-signed X.509 certificate that serves react-scripts-ts/webpack-dev-server's local HTTPS during development (selfsigned ^1.9.1 declared at package-lock.json:22982 and :43666 — the webpack-dev-server entries; selfsigned depends on node-forge@0.9.0 at :19491). DevDependency chain only — never lands in the shipped browser bundle, but it is the TLS posture of the local dev server. Changeable here trivially.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js supplies SHA-256/HMAC-SHA-256 inside @walletconnect/crypto (declared as hash.js ^1.1.7 at package-lock.json:1993) — the derivation/MAC half of the WalletConnect v1 session channel (AES-CBC via aes-js + HMAC via hash.js) that src/App.tsx:176/210 `new WalletConnect(...)` sessions rely on — and is also consumed by elliptic/ethereum-cryptography for the Ethereum crypto stack. It is live in the shipped bundle via the WalletConnect path. Same logical asset as ALG-50e53f84 (SHA family via hash.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The pbkdf2 npm package (Node crypto.pbkdf2 browser shim) ships via the browserify crypto stack — ethereum-cryptography@0.1.3 declares pbkdf2 ^3.0.17 (package-lock.json:6916). One of the packages behind ALG-4de3b020's PBKDF2 sites; the PBKDF2 actually exercised by this app runs inside ethers (@ethersproject/pbkdf2) as the BIP-39 half of ethers.Wallet.fromMnemonic at src/controllers/wallet.ts:95. Available in the shipped library; no first-party call site.
